leading_positions.synthesis: Five of eight members put B037 (Katori and Ye, optical lattice clocks) as their sole preferred prize part, with near-identical two-name credit and citations built on the magic-wavelength lattice and the 10^-18 regime. Shared: a clean concept-to-realisation attribution, independent reproduction, and uses in redshift tests, constants and dark-matter searches. Not shared: how much the 2005 comb prize and 2012 ion-control prize make the work incremental, whether the pending redefinition of the second is a reason to wait, and how to treat NIST, PTB, SYRTE and other lattice-clock groups left outside the two names. Danielsson, Johansson and Olsson moved to B037 from other first choices after the opening exchange, and each ties that move partly to credit problems elsewhere on the shortlist.

Two members prefer B042 (Kane, Mele, Molenkamp, quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators) with a citation tied to the Z2 prediction and the HgTe observation. Both state the credit weakness themselves: Bernevig, Hughes and the late Zhang made the HgTe proposal that the experiment tested, and the 3D work of Fu, Moore, Balents, Hasan and others lies outside the trio. They also share the concern that the 2016 topological-phases prize is adjacent and that edge quantisation is less clean than in the quantum Hall effect. B042 is the most frequently named alternative (danielsson-ulf, johansson-goran, kroll-stefan, lindroth-eva, olsson-eva and mehlig-bernhard list it), but several of those members say the credit gap keeps it from their preferred configuration.

One member prefers B005 (Toner, Ramaswamy, Vicsek, active-matter hydrodynamics) on grounds of conceptual novelty, three decades of theory and quantitative tests, and no prior prize for nonequilibrium collective phenomena. No other member prefers it. Colleagues who comment (danielsson-ulf, lindroth-eva, pearce-mark) raise the omission of Yuhai Tu, the still-contested two-dimensional Toner-Tu exponents and the absence of cross-member support; Mehlig lists B042 and B037 as alternatives and states that the Tu omission is a real defect.

areas_of_agreement: No member prefers B006, B008, B027, B004, B018, B016, B029 or B011 as a sole prize part; the preferred configurations are all single prize parts on B037, B042 or B005.

B037 and B042 are each described by several members as scientifically mature, reproduced by independent groups and prize-worthy in principle; disagreement is mainly about credit and timing, not merit.

Seven members (danielsson-ulf, eriksson-olle, johansson-goran, kroll-stefan, lindroth-eva, olsson-eva, pearce-mark) explicitly state that the Higgs observation (B006) is of the highest scientific significance but that Della Negra, Jenni and Virdee are founders or project leaders rather than identifiable discoverers, so the three-name credit is arbitrary; Mehlig, the eighth member, likewise declines to put B006 in his preferred configuration on practicality grounds. Danielsson, who ranked it first in the opening round, now concedes most of this.

Where a citation is proposed, members favour narrow wording tied to the specific idea (magic-wavelength lattice clocks; the Z2 prediction plus HgTe observation) with adjacent contributors acknowledged in the text.
scientific_disputes: Whether the optical lattice clock is a new principle or an advance in measurement: Lindroth and Olsson see magic-wavelength trapping of ensembles as a conceptual step opening many-body and geodesy applications, while Mehlig asks what new physical principle it adds beyond the magic-wavelength idea, and Pearce, as an instrument builder, sees more novelty in a new class of matter than in improved accuracy.

Whether the 2016 prize on topological phases and transitions substantially overlaps B042: Pearce, Eriksson, Johansson and Kroll treat it as a real adjacency, Danielsson argues time-reversal-invariant Z2 insulators are a distinct idea, and Eriksson and Pearce agree that edge quantisation in HgTe is less clean than in the quantum Hall effect.

Whether the Toner-Tu two-dimensional exponents are established experimentally well enough for B005, or whether the prize should rest on the flocking phase and hydrodynamic framework alone (Mehlig, Pearce, Danielsson).

Whether active matter counts as physics of sufficiently general importance when its best-known realisations are biological or soft-matter systems (raised by Mehlig as a case against his own first choice).
Whether the clustering of AMO and precision-measurement recognition (2005, 2012, 2018, 2022, 2023, 2025) should weigh against B037, B016, B029 and B008 (Mehlig, Lindroth, Olsson, Johansson).
attribution_disputes: B042: whether a Kane, Mele, Molenkamp prize is defensible when the HgTe proposal tested by Molenkamp came from Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang (deceased) and the 3D work of Fu, Moore, Balents and Hasan is outside the trio. Eriksson, Mehlig, Olsson, Johansson, Danielsson, Kroll and Lindroth flag this; Pearce and Eriksson, the preferring members, accept it as the main weakness and propose wording the citation to avoid claiming the whole field.

B006: whether detector founders and project leaders are a defensible proxy for the ATLAS and CMS discovery, or whether any three names from two collaborations of thousands would be arbitrary. Danielsson, who earlier ranked it first, still lists it as an alternative and asks for an expert view on which individuals are decisive.

B037: whether two names suffice given NIST, PTB, SYRTE and other lattice-clock groups and the ion-clock community, and whether Ye should be credited for the lattice clock itself or for clock-comb integration and the accuracy frontier (Kroll, Danielsson).
B005: Yuhai Tu is a co-author of the Toner-Tu theory but is outside the credited set, and Simha, Marchetti and others are also omitted.

B027 and B029: Eriksson and Olsson note that Metzner is outside the B027 credit; Lindroth notes that experimental credit for B029 is unclear given Wineland's earlier prize and the roles of Monroe and others.

Ye's earlier recognition: my own round-1 statement said Ye shared the 2005 prize; Lindroth responded that the 2005 frequency-comb prize went to Hall and Hansch, not Ye. I record that correction here. Danielsson, Johansson and Olsson also frame Ye as part of the 2005 circle of work or comb context, which is a perception or novelty question and not a bar to recognition.
maturity_disputes: B037: whether the redefinition of the second, not yet formally adopted, is a reason to wait. Lindroth, Olsson, Kroll and Danielsson answer that the prize recognises the demonstrated accuracy and independent reproduction; Pearce and, in part, Olsson earlier saw the pending redefinition as a point for waiting.

B018 (magic-angle graphene): Lindroth lists it as an alternative but questions whether the superconducting mechanism is settled; Olsson, who ranked it third in the opening round, now considers it a few years early; Eriksson ranked it as possibly premature.
B005: three decades of theory and quantitative tests are cited in support, but the central two-dimensional exponents remain contested, so members differ on whether this is mature enough.
B008: Johansson, who works in the subfield, notes the 2025 superconducting-circuit prize is recent and that the committee may want more distance before considering circuit QED.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: johansson-goran: directs the Wallenberg Centre for Quantum Technology and works on superconducting and circuit QED at Chalmers, so B008 is in his own subfield and may require recusal or discounting; Chalmers colleagues Per Delsing and C. M. Wilson work on related physics. No documented connection to B037, B042 or B029 candidates.

kroll-stefan: trained in laser spectroscopy at Lund under Sune Svanberg and spent a research stay in John Hall's laboratory; discloses closeness to the field adjacent to B037 (2005 comb prize). No documented tie to Katori or Ye.

lindroth-eva: documents a long-running collaboration with Anne L'Huillier and the Lund group and papers with Ursula Keller's group at ETH Zurich; would consider recusal on B004 (Keller) if it is discussed in depth. Works in atomic theory in the same broad field as B037, B016 and B029 without a documented tie to Katori or Ye.

pearce-mark (chair): background in CERN-based doctoral work and instrument collaborations (PAMELA, Fermi-LAT, PoGO+) gives a general affinity with experimental detector projects such as ATLAS and CMS (B006); no personal tie to those collaborations is recorded, and the committee may decide on recusal.

mehlig-bernhard: active matter and stochastic dynamics lie close to his research interests, but no documented tie to Toner, Ramaswamy or Vicsek; the subject proximity should be discounted accordingly.

eriksson-olle and danielsson-ulf: no specific conflict; Eriksson notes adjacency of his electronic-structure field to B042 and B027 and that he chaired the 2025 cycle, and Danielsson notes limited ability to judge the experimental priority history of B037. olsson-eva: no conflict for the shortlisted IDs, and notes a Chalmers colleague relationship with Johansson.
questions_for_round2: B037: is the committee prepared to treat Ye's 2005 comb-era association as no bar once the record shows Hall and Hansch were the 2005 laureates, and should the premise in the chair's own round-1 statement be withdrawn?

B037: can the citation be worded narrowly around magic-wavelength lattice clocks and the 10^-18 regime so that it is clearly distinct from the 2005 comb prize and the 2012 ion-control prize, and what new principle beyond the magic-wavelength idea does the committee identify for the Statutes' discovery or invention criterion?

B037: does the pending redefinition of the second count as a reason to wait, or as confirmation of maturity, and how are NIST, PTB, SYRTE and other lattice-clock contributors acknowledged outside a two-name prize?

B042: supporters, how would you word a citation that credits the Z2 prediction and the HgTe observation while stating openly that the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal and the 3D work are outside it, and do members who list B042 as an alternative accept that wording as defensible given Zhang's death?

B042: does the 2016 prize on topological phases and transitions overlap enough to count against a quantum spin Hall prize, and does the less clean quantisation of the helical edge weaken the experimental half?

B006: can any member propose a principled, defensible three-person rule across ATLAS and CMS, or an expert view on which individuals are decisive; if not, do members agree that B006 cannot be a person-based prize at this stage?
B005: can Yuhai Tu's omission and the unsettled two-dimensional exponents be reconciled with a three-person credit, and does any member other than mehlig-bernhard see a route to majority support?

Across the shortlist: with five members preferring B037, two preferring B042 and one preferring B005, which unresolved credit or timing problem would change each member's preferred prize part, and would any member move to a different candidate if it were resolved?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 leaves a main split between B037, with a clean two-name credit but contested novelty relative to earlier AMO prizes, and B042, with clear scientific maturity but an incomplete credit set, plus a single-member case for B005. Members' stated reasons for preferring one over the other are mostly about attribution and recency, not about the quality of the science, and several first-round positions shifted after the opening exchange. The Higgs observation is widely described as scientifically compelling but is not preferred by any member. The chair does not rule on any of these points and has corrected one factual premise in his own statement about the 2005 prize.
